extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in category theory, homological algebra, and algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts definitions, axioms, and standard constructions in category theory, homological algebra, and convenient categories of topology (e.g., resolutions, kernels/cokernels, (co)products, closed and enriched categories, compactly generated spaces, biproducts, additive and abelian categories). Useful as a reference when proving results or computing homology/cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard (free) resolution of the trivial group module
rubrics_metrics.description: The augmented simplicial object (Smp L)Z with An = Z(G) ⊗ ··· ⊗ Z(G) (n-fold tensor) gives an augmented chain complex in G-Mod which is a 'free resolution' of the trivial G-module Z; this is the standard resolution used to define the homology and cohomology of the group G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit generators are x ⊗ x1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ xn written x[x1|···|xn]; the G-module structure and explicit face and degeneracy operators are given (face maps di and degeneracies si), and this resolution may be used to construct derived functors such as group (co)homology (see Mac Lane [1963]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing group cohomology via Hom
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the functor Hom_G(-, A): (G-Mod)^{op} → Ab to the standard resolution (dropping augmentation) to obtain a cochain complex whose coboundary is b = Hom_G(δ, A); its cohomology groups are H^n(G, A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-degree interpretations: H^0(G,A) = {a ∈ A | xa = a for all x}; H^1(G,A) is crossed homomorphisms modulo principal crossed homomorphisms; H^2(G,A) classifies group extensions of A by G with conjugation from the G-module structure. The face formulas give explicit coboundary formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing group homology via tensor
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the (covariant, additive) functor C ⊗_G - (for a right G-module C) to the standard resolution to obtain a chain complex; its homology groups are H_n(G, C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: H_0(G, Z) = Z and H_1(G, Z) = G/[G,G] (the abelianization). Reference: Mac Lane [1963], Prop. X.5.1 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric monoidal category (symmetry conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A monoidal category B is symmetric when equipped with natural isomorphisms γ_{a,b}: a ⊗ b ≅ b ⊗ a such that certain coherence diagrams commute (including γ_{a,b} o γ_{b,a} = id and compatibility with associativity/unit constraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed selection of coherence conditions suffices (Mac Lane [1963b]) to prove that all such diagrams commute, analogous to the coherence theorem. Monoidal categories where ⊗ is categorical product or coproduct are automatically symmetric with the canonical swap commuting with projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed category
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed category V is a symmetric monoidal category in which each functor - ⊗ b: V → V has a specified right adjoint ( )^b: V → V (an 'internal hom').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (Ab, ⊗, -) is closed with internal hom AB = Hom(B, A); (K-Mod, ⊗_K, ...) is closed for any commutative ring K; cartesian closed categories (Set, Cat) are closed. The internal hom gives an enriched notion of hom-objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: B-category / enriched category over B
rubrics_metrics.description: A B-category consists of objects r,s,t; for each pair (r,s) an object R(r,s) ∈ B; composition arrows R(s,t) ⊗ R(r,s) → R(r,t); and unit arrows e → R(r,r) in B, satisfying associativity and unit axioms (i.e., composition and units expressed inside B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structure does not by itself yield ordinary hom-sets; applying a functor U: B → Set (e.g., U = B(e,-)) produces hom-sets U R(r,s). Most of the basic theory of categories applies to enriched categories provided B is closed. References: Dubuc [1970], Kelly [1982].

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of compactly generated (Kelley) space
rubrics_metrics.description: A topological space X is compactly generated when every subset A ⊆ X that intersects every compact subset C of X in a closed set is itself closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGHaus denotes compactly generated Hausdorff spaces (Kelley spaces). Metrizable spaces and locally compact Hausdorff spaces are compactly generated. This property is chosen so that categorical products have right adjoints (function spaces) in the restricted category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kelleyfication (coreflection) K Y of a Hausdorff space Y
rubrics_metrics.description: K Y has the same points as Y and a subset A ⊆ Y is closed in K Y iff A ∩ C is closed in Y for every compact C ⊆ Y; the identity B_Y: K Y → Y is continuous and K Y is Hausdorff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any continuous map f: X → Y from a compactly generated X, f factors uniquely as X → K Y → Y; this universal property makes CGHaus a full coreflective subcategory of Haus. Kelleyfication preserves limits (right adjoint), so CGHaus is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: CGHaus is a full coreflective subcategory of Haus
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion CGHaus → Haus is full and has a right adjoint K (Kelleyfication): for Hausdorff Y, K Y is compactly generated, same points, and identity K Y → Y is the co-unit of the adjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness/factorization property: any continuous map from a compactly generated X to Y factors through K Y, giving the universal property. Closed (or open) subspaces of CGHaus are in CGHaus; coproducts in Haus of compactly generated spaces remain compactly generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: CGHaus is complete and cocomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: CGHaus has all small limits and colimits: completeness follows because Haus is complete and the right adjoint K preserves limits; cocompleteness is shown e.g., by showing coequalizers in Haus of maps between CGHaus objects lie in CGHaus (via Kelleyfication argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, product in CGHaus is K(X × Y) (Kelleyfication of ordinary product). Coproducts (disjoint unions) of compactly generated spaces are compactly generated; coequalizers can be constructed and then Kelleyfied if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: CGHaus is cartesian closed (function-space adjunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For compactly generated Hausdorff spaces X and Y, define X^Y = K(Cop(Y,X)) (Kelleyfication of compact-open topology). The evaluation map e: X^Y × Y → X is continuous and universal, giving the adjunction CGHaus(Z × Y, X) ≅ CGHaus(Z, X^Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove continuity of evaluation it suffices to check on compact sets and use subbase N(C,U) for Cop(Y,X). This adjunction yields the desired bijection/homeomorphism of function spaces; the category is cartesian closed. If Y is locally compact Hausdorff, the compact-open topology suffices without Kelleyfication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smash product, suspension, and loop-space adjunction in pointed CGHaus*
rubrics_metrics.description: In pointed compactly generated Hausdorff spaces, the smash product Z ∧ Y = (Z × Y)/[(Z × *) ∪ (* × Y)] gives an adjunction CGHaus*(Z ∧ Y, X) ≅ CGHaus*(Z, X^Y_*) where X^Y_* denotes basepoint-preserving maps. The reduced suspension Σ and loop functor Ω satisfy Σ ⊣ Ω (Σ left adjoint to Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: ΣX = X ∧ S^1 (reduced suspension), ΩX = Map_*(S^1, X) (loop space). Example: Σ S^n = S^{n+1}; units and counits of adjunctions have geometric interpretations. Iteration yields Σ^n ⊣ Ω^n and Ω^n preserves products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel in a category with a null object
rubrics_metrics.description: In a category with a null object, a kernel of an arrow f: a → b is an equalizer of f and the zero map a → b; equivalently k: s → a satisfies f k = 0 and any h with f h = 0 factors uniquely through k. A kernel is necessarily monic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in Grp, kernel is the usual subgroup of elements sent to identity (normal subgroup); in Set_* the kernel is the subset of points mapping to basepoint. In Ab-categories, equalizers are kernels because Hom-sets are abelian groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cokernel and Galois connection between kernels and cokernels
rubrics_metrics.description: Given kernels and cokernels in a category with null object, the relations 'g factors through f' on arrows with fixed domain/codomain define preorders; kernel and cokernel operations define a Galois connection between these preorders, yielding identities like ker(coker(ker u)) = ker u and coker(ker(coker f)) = coker f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From these identities, an arrow g is a kernel iff g = ker(coker g). These triangular identities parallel familiar algebraic dualities and are useful when reasoning about canonical factorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical epi–monic factorization via kernels and cokernels
rubrics_metrics.description: Any arrow f has a canonical factorization f = m q where m = ker(coker f) and q = coker(ker f); under further hypotheses (equalizers exist and every monic is a kernel), q is an epimorphism, so f factors as epi followed by monic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma: if f = m' q' with m' a kernel then there is a unique diagonal t with m = m' t and q' = t q; and if monics are kernels and equalizers exist then q is epi (proof uses equalizer arguments). This yields the standard epi–mono factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ab-category (Ab-enriched category)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Ab-category is a category in which each hom-set A(b,c) is an abelian group and composition of arrows is bilinear relative to this addition (i.e., addition distributes over composition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such a category a zero element 0: b → c exists for each hom-set, and a null object (initial ≡ terminal) is equivalent to A(z,z) being the zero group. Many familiar categories (Ab, R-Mod, Mod-R) are Ab-categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biproduct diagram and equivalence of product and coproduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A biproduct diagram for objects a,b is an object c with injections i1,i2 and projections p1,p2 satisfying p1 i1 = 1_a, p2 i2 = 1_b, and i1 p1 + i2 p2 = 1_c (together with p_k i_j = 0 for k ≠ j). In an Ab-category, a and b have a product iff they have a biproduct; dually the biproduct is also a coproduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a biproduct, the object c with projections is a product and with injections is a coproduct. Biproducts give matrix calculus for arrows: arrows between finite biproducts are matrices of components and composition is matrix multiplication. Iteration yields n-ary biproducts with standard identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive category and additive functor
rubrics_metrics.description: An additive category is an Ab-category with a zero object and biproducts for every pair of objects. An additive functor T: A → B is a functor between Ab-categories that preserves addition of parallel arrows: T(f+g) = Tf + Tg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, if A has all binary biproducts, T is additive iff it carries each binary biproduct diagram in A to a biproduct diagram in B (hence additive functors preserve biproducts, products, coproducts). Examples: Hom-functors A(a,-), tensor products, and torsion product functors are additive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of addition from biproducts
rubrics_metrics.description: In an additive category the sum of parallel arrows f, f' : a → b can be expressed in terms of biproduct structure by f + f' = ∇_b ◦ (f ⊕ f') ◦ Δ_a, where Δ_a: a → a ⊕ a is diagonal and ∇_b: b ⊕ b → b is codiagonal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows the additive structure of Hom-sets can be derived from biproduct structure; Proposition 3 gives the explicit formula and justifies that additive structure is encoded by biproducts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of abelian category (axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian category A is an Ab-category satisfying: (i) A has a null object; (ii) A has binary biproducts; (iii) every arrow in A has a kernel and a cokernel; (iv) every monic is a kernel and every epi is a cokernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms suffice to reproduce homological algebra arguments analogous to those in Ab (chasing elements replaced by diagram arguments). They characterize categories like Ab, R-Mod, Mod-R, and R-Mod-S.
